competitive_landscape: Public marine transport is limited — private boats to Amwaj, dhow tours, and leisure craft. The Gulf neighbours are reached by air or, for Saudi Arabia, the chronically congested King Fahd Causeway. For an island nation at the centre of the Gulf, there is no fast water network either within the archipelago or across to its neighbours — a structural gap.

regulatory_note: Marine activity falls under Bahrain's Ports and Maritime Affairs, within GCC cabotage rules; the King Fahd Causeway congestion gives a clear public-interest case for a cross-Gulf marine corridor.
seasonality: The sheltered inner archipelago is operable year-round; summer (Jun–Sep) is hot and humid but calm, winter (Oct–Apr) is peak with occasional shamal chop that foiling smooths. Cross-Gulf corridors track the calmer winter window.

summary: Bahrain is an archipelago: Manama, Muharraq, Amwaj, Diyar, Reef Island and the Hawar group are all natural water-mobility nodes. Its position mid-Gulf makes it the connective hub of the region — Dammam, Doha, Dubai and Abu Dhabi are all reachable as single hybrid legs, while the inner islands suit all-electric hops.
tagline: An island nation at the center of the Gulf — every neighbor a single leg away.
transit_planning: For an authority: a premium, zero-emission inter-island marine layer that relieves causeway peaks, plus a credible Gulf inter-city corridor — additive to existing transport.
